recall_prompt: Say how you would find the multiplicative inverse — what the inverse is, and how you write it as a + ib.
insider_note: The trap is answering with the conjugate √5 − 3i itself — the inverse is 1/z, and the conjugate is only the multiplier. (√5)² is 5, not 25, so the denominator is 5 + 9 = 14.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the reciprocal
steps.margin_note: First mark. The multiplicative inverse of z is 1/z. Multiply above and below by the conjugate √5 − 3i; the denominator becomes (√5)² + 3² = 5 + 9.

recall.must_convey: That the multiplicative inverse is 1/(√5 + 3i), and multiplying top and bottom by √5 − 3i makes the denominator 5 + 9.
accept: the inverse is one over root five plus three i, multiply top and bottom by root five minus three i
write one by z and rationalise with the conjugate root five minus three i
the denominator becomes root five squared plus three squared which is five plus nine
inverse ante one by z, conjugate root five minus three i tho multiply cheyali
multiplicative inverse is the reciprocal, rationalise it

steps.why: The inverse is 1/z because z · (1/z) = 1. The conjugate makes the denominator (√5)² + 3² = 14, a real number, and the square root disappears from the bottom.
common_mistakes: Giving the conjugate √5 − 3i itself as the inverse.
Writing (√5)² as √25 or as 25 instead of 5.

steps.label: Simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 5 + 9 = 14. Separate the real and imaginary parts.

recall.must_convey: That the denominator is 14, so the inverse is √5/14 − (3/14)i.
accept: five plus nine is fourteen so the inverse is root five by fourteen minus three by fourteen i
the answer is root five minus three i over fourteen
root five by fourteen minus three i by fourteen
denominator fourteen, inverse root five by fourteen minus three by fourteen i
divide root five minus three i by fourteen

steps.why: The answer is in the form a + ib once the real part √5/14 and the imaginary part −3/14 are visible. The √5 stays in the numerator — it does not simplify further.
common_mistakes: Trying to 'rationalise' the √5 in the numerator — it is already in simplest form.
